messages:
alice: FYI we just saw two PROD pods OOM during a 50k-token replay test. Node logs show attention-kv growth and heavy paging to host memory before the oom kill.
ben: ugh. which model/quantization?
alice: rtx-40q, q4_0, 2-shard config. the runtime had kernel fallback enabled for some ops.
carla: can you paste the OOM stack/log?
alice: here's the tail: 
```
OOM killed process 2345 (redwood-infer)
Signal 9: rss peaked at 112GB
alloc failed in kvstore.cpp:reserve_segment() at 0x7f2a1c
backtrace: runtime::allocate_kv_segment -> kvstore::page_to_host -> kernel_fallback::dispatch
```
dmitri: hmm kernel_fallback::dispatch implies some optimized kernels hit an unsupported path and we paged out kv pages. batching heuristics might've increased live KV entries.
ben: did the batching window spike? any slow clients?
alice: yes, there was a client burst with 8 concurrent long-history chats causing batching to group long sequences. avg seq-length in that window ~42k -> kv entries blew up.
carla: can we confirm whether prefix caching was enabled? That changes reuse behavior.
alice: prefix caching = on. reusage was high but eviction couldn't keep up because our paging threshold was conservative and the host swap throttled.
ops-oncall: infra-bot reported disk I/O saturation around same time, which likely slowed page-out and made memory pressure worse.
dmitri: two mitigation ideas: 1) immediate runtime hotfix to lower batchable sequence cap and cap concurrent long requests, 2) fallback policy to disable attention-kv on long sessions and use streaming recompute.
ben: agree. also add fast path: if kv memory > X% of GPU we proactively evict least-recently-used spans and force async copy-to-host with backpressure to the request queue.
carla: can we do graceful degradation instead of outright OOM? e.g. return 503 with Retry-After or reroute to a smaller model instance.
alice: prototyping a short patch: if estimated-kv-bytes > 0.7 * gpu-memory then set request->kv_mode = RECOMPUTE and annotate response header. snippet: 
```
if (kv_est > gpu_mem * 0.7) {
  req->kv_mode = KV_MODE_RECOMPUTE;
  req->meta.add("x-rw-reason", "kv-pressure");
}
```
dmitri: nice. add telemetry counters and a debug trace so we can see how often we flip to recompute. also record batch sizes when flips happen.
ben: long-term we should revisit kernel selection: the fallback path is cheaper in compute but expensive in memory movement. maybe prefer kernels that trade more compute for lower persistent KV. also revisit quantization placement — some kernel combos inflate KV layout.
carla: for immediate deploy, propose: reduce max_merge_window from 50ms to 10ms for long-seq routes, enable early eviction threshold at 60% gpu, and enable recompute fallback on threshold breach.
ops-oncall: rolling patch staged to canary now. infra-bot: canary deploy started on prod-canary cluster.
alice: after canary we saw 3x fewer kv spikes and no OOMs in 24h. still seeing slight perf regression (~8% latency p95) for affected traffic.
dmitri: expected tradeoff. open follow-ups: (1) perf-regression eval vs cost savings (2) kernel selection matrix for long-context workloads (3) persistent vs ephemeral kv partitioning experiment.
carla: created ticket INF-4821 with the notes and assigned to eng-runtime. tagging @sre for SLA impact.
ben: thanks team. next steps: instrument more detailed KV fragmentation histograms so we can decide eviction granularity.
alice: adding flamegraph and nvprof outputs to the ticket. attaching sample metrics: kv_pages_allocated: 12k, avg_page_reuse_distance: 18, tail_copy_latency_ms: 420.
ops-oncall: monitoring alerts updated to fire a soft-warning at 50% kv usage (not just 80%).
infra-bot: incident resolved: mitigation deployed, monitoring green. :white_check_mark:
